response.reason: After checking all 8 numbered NL segments against the 21 primary contracts and 10 transition groups, every independently violable obligation is already represented. The NL describes a flat state machine with six states, one initial entry, fifteen transitions (including one self-loop), two state actions (cooking time displayed/updated in ReadytoCook, timer starts in Cooking), and two transition effects (cancel/update cooking time on ReadytoCook-to-DoorShutWithItem, stop timer on Cooking-to-DoorOpenWithItem). No segment establishes explicit containment hierarchy, termination/completion semantics, deadlock-freedom or progress requirements, event-consumer coverage across a scope, guard-disjointness (all alternatives are distinguished by different events, not competing guards on the same event), state-retention, reachability beyond what the transitions themselves imply, or any additional variable-delta obligation. The "zero time set" qualifier in NL4 is a branch-selection condition preserved on the transition-group alternative and does not independently require a separate formal guard contract at NL extraction.
